newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Motorola opens cellular plant in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Motorola opens cellular plant in Brazil.

text.p: Motorola Inc opened its first cellular phone assembly plant in Latin America today, with an eye to supplying the fast-growing Brazilian and Mercosur markets, a company official said.

"Brazil is one of the world's fastest growing markets and can only be compared to China," Wolf Pavlov, Motorola senior vice-president and general manager of the America's subscribers group, said at a news conference.
Pavlov said Motorola's decision to open an assembly plant in Brazil was prompted by the country's decision to offer Band B frequency concessions in 1997.

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's administration has said it is committed to privatizing the country's telecommunications system, Latin America's largest, but has been slow in laying out a detailed blueprint for the selloff.
Brazil accounts for 50 percent of all the Latin American cellular phone market and demand for cell phones is expected to jump to 10 million units in 1999 from the present two million.
The $20 million Motorola plant in Jaguariuna, a small town 80 miles (130 kms) from the city of Sao Paulo, will employ 250 people and assemble DPC650j and Lite II cellular phone models.
